=== file .claude/CLAUDE.md
<!-- cartographer:instructions:begin — block managed by Cartographer, do not edit by hand -->
<!-- cartographer:kb:kb-a:begin -->
The "kb-a" KB is served via MCP by the "cartographer" server. No maps yet.

Skills: notes, review.
<!-- cartographer:kb:kb-a:end -->

Operational instructions:
- consult it autonomously when you need historical or architectural context: `search` (keyword) or `atlas_overview` to orient yourself, `concept_read` to read; when the answer spans several linked pages, `graph_context` ranks them in one call instead of reading page by page and following links;
- write or update a page with `concept_write` when you discover something relevant; close relevant sessions with `log_append`;
- a write that would introduce an avoidable finding (broken link, missing index entry, orphan) is refused with each finding's fix and nothing is committed: write the target, the index entry and the link in the same `concept_batch`;
- status convention: `active` means the page is valid and current, not that work is open; open work uses `open` (accepted or queued, not started), `in-progress` or `blocked`: when you start executing an `open` item, set `in-progress` in the same `concept_patch` or `concept_batch` that records the first progress; when progress cannot continue, set `blocked` and declare `waiting_on` and `review_after`; a finished task is `done`;
- every write is a git commit, revertible.
- never run git commands in the KB's clone: report replication problems from `sync_status` to the operator instead; a push refused because of the commits' author is reported with the command `cartographer kb reauthor <kb>`, for the operator to run.
- when `kb_status` reports a `latest_version` that differs from `server_version`, tell the user once: the installed version, the available version and the upgrade command for this channel (`cartographer update check` prints it); offer to run it, run it only on explicit consent, then follow the cartographer-ops skill (§Upgrade).
- a question about how Cartographer itself works (command, flag, key, error, why) goes to the `cartographer-docs` skill (`cartographer docs graph_context query="<content words>"`), never to memory;
- on a likely defect in Cartographer (an internal error, behaviour that contradicts the docs, a limit you must work around, a user complaint), offer once per problem and per session, if the user agrees, a report via the `cartographer-feedback` skill; never file or offer silently;
- procedures, runbooks and incidents are read whole with `concept_read`, never answered from a search excerpt or a snippet;
- `kb_guide` returns the full operating guide, each KB's own directives and its skills with descriptions, on demand: call it when a task touches a KB's own rules or when a skill name in a `Skills:` line looks relevant (on a routed connection it takes the `kb` argument like every tool).

Subagents installed by the "kb-a" KB: auditor, explorer — their descriptions are in the client's agent registry: delegate to them the tasks they cover.
<!-- cartographer:instructions:end -->
